title: Attack, finish development or defend: one count, three choices
outcomes: Chooses between attacking, improving first (finishing development) and defending by counting attackers and defenders at the target
Checks whether an attacker of his is loose before answering it passively
Answers an early queen or knight raid with a move that develops with gain of time or wins the loose piece
Says that a development lead licensing an attack is a rule of thumb

steps.text: In **Count before you attack: attack now, not yet, or no** you counted at one target. Now there are three honest choices: **attack**, **improve first** (finish development, or bring up a rook), or **defend**. Count the attackers and defenders at the target first. Then ask two more questions: is one of *your* pieces loose, and is his attack too early? This lesson adds the choice, not the count.

steps.caption: White brought the queen out on move two. Black has just played g6.

line.say: The queen retreats. Black's pawn move attacked it, so Black gained a move.
Black develops a knight with that free move.

claims.statement: One black piece attacks the queen on h5: the pawn on g6.

steps.text: **Attack** when the count favours you or a concrete tactic wins material; the count alone is a **rule of thumb** with exceptions. **Improve first** when the count is level and a quiet move (development, a rook, a queen move that adds pressure) adds an attacker. **Defend** when his threat is real; first check whether his attacker is loose. A development lead licensing an attack is a **rule of thumb**: it fails when he has already developed.
